steps.title: Deliver config/accounts-config.yaml with the three mandatory LZA accounts (sunstonesecure.com emails, spec-aligned descriptions) and empty workloadAccounts
steps.intent: Deliver, at the repository-root config/accounts-config.yaml, the LZA accounts-config declaring EXACTLY the three mandatory accounts — Management (organizationalUnit Root), LogArchive and Audit (both organizationalUnit Security) — each carrying the spec section 6.5 canonical description and an email in valid EmailAddress form on the operator's real sunstonesecure.com domain, tagged with the test-turtle-1 repository name (management+test-turtle-1@sunstonesecure.com, logarchive+test-turtle-1@sunstonesecure.com, audit+test-turtle-1@sunstonesecure.com), with workloadAccounts as an empty list (issue #117; LZACFG-010..013). The operator judged v1 and chose option (c) on q-already-delivered — apply a specific content change — so this is NOT the no-op re-affirmation of the file already on main: the delivered file replaces the prior example.com placeholder emails with sunstonesecure.com addresses (corrections #119 and #120 and answer q-emails) and aligns the LogArchive and Audit descriptions to spec section 6.5 (answer q-descriptions). The emails still deploy nothing under the Phase 0 credential-free posture (REQ-049/REQ-051); they are real-format addresses that satisfy the pinned LZA v1.16.1 EmailAddress schema. The prototype under inputs/lza-phase0/ is read-only reference; the reserved machinery (.github/**, scripts/**, schemas/**, dashboard/**, package manifests) and the governance record (plans/**, confirmations/**, evidence/**) are out of scope and must not be touched.
steps.acceptance: config/accounts-config.yaml exists at the repository root, parses as YAML, declares exactly three mandatoryAccounts mapping name to organizationalUnit as {Management: Root, LogArchive: Security, Audit: Security}, each account carries its spec section 6.5 canonical description and an email of the form <name>+test-turtle-1@sunstonesecure.com on the sunstonesecure.com domain (no example.com placeholder and no ${...} token), and workloadAccounts is an empty list.

verification_targets.check: config/accounts-config.yaml declares exactly the three mandatory accounts mapping name to organizationalUnit as {Management: Root, LogArchive: Security, Audit: Security}, workloadAccounts is an empty list, and every account email is on the operator-directed sunstonesecure.com domain (LZACFG-010..013; corrections #119/#120).
verification_targets.run: python3 -c 'import yaml; a=yaml.safe_load(open("config/accounts-config.yaml")); ma=a["mandatoryAccounts"]; m={x["name"]:x["organizationalUnit"] for x in ma}; assert m=={"Management":"Root","LogArchive":"Security","Audit":"Security"}, m; assert a["workloadAccounts"]==[]; assert all(str(x.get("email","")).endswith("@sunstonesecure.com") for x in ma), [x.get("email") for x in ma]'

verification_targets.check: Each of the three mandatory accounts has an email of the operator-directed form <name>+test-turtle-1@sunstonesecure.com — valid EmailAddress form on the sunstonesecure.com domain carrying the test-turtle-1 repository-name tag, never a ${...} token and never an example.com placeholder (correction #120; answer q-emails).
verification_targets.run: python3 -c 'import re,yaml; a=yaml.safe_load(open("config/accounts-config.yaml")); pat=re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+\+test-turtle-1@sunstonesecure\.com$"); ma=a["mandatoryAccounts"]; assert len(ma)==3, len(ma); assert all(pat.match(str(x.get("email",""))) for x in ma), [x.get("email") for x in ma]'

verification_targets.check: Each of the three mandatory accounts carries its spec section 6.5 canonical description: Management 'GovCloud organization management account', LogArchive 'AWS Control Tower and platform log archive account', Audit 'AWS Control Tower security, Config aggregator, and audit account' (answer q-descriptions).
verification_targets.run: python3 -c 'import yaml; a=yaml.safe_load(open("config/accounts-config.yaml")); d={x["name"]:x["description"] for x in a["mandatoryAccounts"]}; assert d=={"Management":"GovCloud organization management account","LogArchive":"AWS Control Tower and platform log archive account","Audit":"AWS Control Tower security, Config aggregator, and audit account"}, d'

boundary_cases.description: config/accounts-config.yaml already existed on main (delivered by the prior workload lza-phase0-1-redo, PR #116) with example.com placeholder emails. The operator judged v1 and directed a content change (q-already-delivered option c; correction #119): the delivered file MUST use the operator's real sunstonesecure.com domain, not example.com. Because the delivered emails — and the spec section 6.5-aligned LogArchive/Audit descriptions — differ from what is on the frozen plan tree, this step now performs real, verifiable work: every verification target is written to fail on the pre-change tree, so this is no longer the no-op the v1 proposal warned of and build-verify should not report action_required.

config/accounts-config.yaml must declare EXACTLY three mandatoryAccounts — no fourth account and none omitted. A build that adds or drops an account fails delivery even if each account present is individually valid.

Emails MUST be in valid EmailAddress form on the operator's real sunstonesecure.com domain, tagged with the test-turtle-1 repository name (e.g. logarchive+test-turtle-1@sunstonesecure.com) — not example.com placeholders and not ${MANAGEMENT_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}-style tokens (correction #120; answer q-emails). LZA v1.16.1 offline validation rejects ${...} tokens; the sunstonesecure.com addresses satisfy the schema while provisioning nothing under the Phase 0 credential-free posture.
